title: Case study: the River Nile and the Aswan High Dam

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: A river’s opportunities, its hazards and how they are managed, for the Nile in Egypt.

blocks.heading: Opportunities and management
blocks.text: The River Nile brings water to a desert country. The Aswan High Dam in southern Egypt, completed in 1970, holds back Lake Nasser. The lake stores water, so farmers downstream can irrigate their fields all year and grow more than one crop a year, and the dam generates hydro-electric power for Egypt’s towns and industry.

blocks.heading: Hazards, then and now
blocks.text: Before the dam, the Nile flooded the valley every year. The dam now controls the flood. It also traps the silt the flood once spread over the farmland, so farmers use artificial fertiliser instead, and with less sediment reaching the sea, parts of the delta coast are being eroded.
